spec.title: Interactive Flask Dashboard with Real-Time Charts and Filters
spec.summary: A production-ready Flask web application delivering an interactive dashboard featuring real‑time charts, data‑driven widgets, and dynamic filtering controls. The UI leverages Chart.js to render responsive visualizations, while the Flask backend exposes RESTful endpoints that serve JSON datasets for each widget. Users can manipulate filter controls to instantly update charts without page reloads, ensuring a seamless analytical experience.

files.name: app.py
files.purpose: Defines the Flask application, routing logic for the dashboard page, multiple RESTful API endpoints providing JSON data for charts and widgets, error handling, and configuration of static and template directories.

files.name: requirements.txt
files.purpose: Lists all third‑party Python packages required for running the application, including Flask, pandas for data manipulation, pytest for testing, requests for external HTTP calls, and any other dependencies like Chart.js if served locally.

files.name: templates/index.html
files.purpose: Full HTML5 UI structure for the dashboard, incorporating a navigation bar, responsive grid layout for widgets, placeholder canvas elements for Chart.js graphs, filter controls, and script tags linking to static CSS and JS assets.

files.name: static/style.css
files.purpose: Provides comprehensive styling for the dashboard layout, widgets, navigation, filter components, and visual enhancements such as responsive design, color themes, hover states, and accessibility considerations.

files.name: static/app.js
files.purpose: Implements client‑side JavaScript to fetch JSON data from Flask API endpoints, initialize Chart.js charts for each widget, handle filter changes, update charts in real time, and manage user interaction events across the dashboard UI.

files.name: test_app.py
files.purpose: Contains a suite of pytest tests that verify the Flask application returns a 200 status for the root route, each API endpoint returns valid JSON, no unhandled exceptions occur during requests, and that the data structures match expected formats.

acceptance_criteria: GET / returns HTTP 200 and serves the dashboard template without errors.
Each API endpoint (e.g., /api/sales, /api/users) returns JSON with correct structure and status 200.
Client‑side JavaScript fetches data from APIs and renders at least two charts accurately.
Filter controls on the dashboard trigger data refreshes and update chart displays without page reloads.
All pytest tests in test_app.py execute successfully, confirming endpoint reliability and data integrity.
assumptions_made: Assumed project type: interactive web dashboard
Assumed stack: Python Flask with HTML5 UI
